column2: Standing, one should recite five lakhs to the right form of the god; at the end of the recitation the ghee oblation should be ten thousand.
The mantra thus nourished may be made to do subjugation, banishing and the like. Empty above, empty below, empty in the middle, free of disease —
the twice-born who knows the three voids is surely freed. One who does not know the Prasada, the great body of five mantras,
endowed with thirty-eight parts, is not called a teacher; he who knows Omkara, Gayatri, Rudra and the rest is the guru.
When sin is done, oblation with sesame and recitation of the Gayatri are declared; having repeated the Gayatri a thousand times, fasting, he is a sin-destroyer.
A cow-killer, father-killer, mother-killer, Brahmin-killer, violator of the teacher's bed, Brahmin-killer, gold-thief, liquor-drinker — by a lakh of recitations
he is purified; or having bathed one should recite a hundred in the water. Having drunk water with a hundred Gayatris one becomes a sin-destroyer.
The Gayatri recited a hundred times is remembered as sin-quieting; recited a thousand times that goddess destroys minor sins;
recited a crore she gives what is desired; one attains divinity and kingship. Having first uttered Omkara, then "bhur bhuvah svah" likewise,
the Gayatri, and Pranava at the end — this is the stated form in recitation. Vishvamitra is the seer, the meter Gayatri, and Savitri;
the deity; in initiation, in recitation and in oblation is the application: Agni, Vayu, Ravi, Vidyut, Yama, the lord of waters, Guru,
Parjanya, Indra, Gandharva, Pusha next, Mitra, Varuna, Tvashtri, the Vasus, the Maruts, the Moon,
Angiras, the Vishvedevas, the Ashvins, Ka, and all gods; Rudra, Brahma and Vishnu are in order the deities of the syllables;
at the time of Gayatri recitation they are told as sin-destroyers. Great toes of feet, ankles, shins, knees,
thighs, genital, testicles, waist, navel, belly, breasts, heart, neck, mouth, palate, nose,
eyes, between the brows, forehead, the east face, the right and left sides, head and mouth in order:
yellow, dark, tawny, emerald, fire-like, gold, lightning, smoky, black, red, fair, sapphire-hued;
crystal, golden, pale, ruby, all-radiant, golden, smoky, red, blue, red, black, golden-hued;
white, black, palasha-colored — these are the colors of the Gayatri in order. At the time of meditation she removes sin; oblation to her gives all desires.
Oblation of sesame with the Gayatri destroys all sin. One desiring peace should do it with barley, one desiring life with ghee,
with mustard seed for success of works, with milk for Brahmic radiance; desiring a son likewise with curds, desiring grain with rice,
with fuel sticks of milk-trees for quieting planetary affliction; desiring wealth with bilva, desiring prosperity with lotuses,
desiring health with durva grass; in grave portents that same; desiring good fortune with guggulu, a student with pudding;
by ten thousand the stated success results, by a lakh what the mind desires; by a crore he is freed from Brahmin-killing and becomes Hari, saver of the family.
Or oblation beginning with the planet-sacrifice, by ten thousand it brings wealth. Then one should practice the invocation of the Gayatri and Omkara;
having remembered Omkara one should bind the top-knot with the Gayatri; having rinsed again one should touch heart, navel and shoulders.
The seer of Pranava is Brahma, the meter Gayatri, the deity Agni, the Supreme Self; its application is in all rites.
The goddess is white, fire-faced, of Katyayana gotra, choosing the three worlds, divine, joined with the earth as support,

the goddess bearing a rosary, seated in a lotus posture, auspicious. "Om, you are radiance, you are greatness, you are strength, you are splendor, you are the abode of the gods; you are the universe, universal life, all, all-life. Om, come, boon-giving goddess; be near me in recitation."
Of all the vyahritis the seer is Prajapati; separately and together the Brahma-syllable is Om.
Vishvamitra, Jamadagni, Bharadvaja, Gautama, Atri, Vasishtha and Kashyapa are in order the seers;
Agni, Vayu, Ravi, Vakpati, Varuna, Indra and Vishnu are in order the deities of the vyahritis.
Gayatri, Ushnih, Anushtubh, Brihati, Pankti, Trishtubh and Jagati — the meters, they say, in order.
In the application of the vyahritis, in breath-control and in oblation, with the verse "Apo hi shtha" or "Drupadadiva" it is remembered;
likewise at the end with the Hiranyavarna and Pavamani verses; one should throw eight drops upward, conquering sin done since birth.
Within the water, with "Rtam ca" and so on, thrice the Aghamarshana. For the verses "Apo hi shtha" the seer is remembered as Sindhudvipa;
for Brahma-bathing its meter is Gayatri, the deity water; the application is in sprinkling and in the Hayavabhritha of the sacrifice.
For the Aghamarshana hymn the seer is Aghamarshana; the meter would be Anushtubh; the deity is Bhavavritta.
Apo jyoti raso is remembered as the head of the Gayatri; its seer is Prajapati; being a yajus it has no meter;
Brahma, Agni, Vayu and Surya are declared the deities. By restraint of breath there is Vayu; from Vayu Agni is born;
from Agni water; then purity; then one should perform the rinsing. "Within, he moves in beings, in the cave, in the universal forms;"
austerity, sacrifice, vashat-call, waters, light, essence, nectar. For "Ud u tyam jatavedasam" the seer is called Prashkanva;
the meter is declared Gayatri, and the deity Surya; the application is in the Atiratra; Agni-Soma is the application;
for the verse "Chitram devanam" the seer is said to be Kutsa; the meter Trishtubh; its deity is declared Surya.
Varenyam — best of all radiances, the supreme abode, always to be chosen by those desiring heaven and liberation;
from the root vri in the sense of choosing: free of waking, dream and the rest, ever pure, awake, one, true — we meditate on that Lord.
I am Brahman, supreme light; we would meditate for liberation. That light is the Lord Vishnu, cause of the world's birth and the rest;
some read Shiva; some read it in the form of Shakti; some the Sun, some Agni — the Veda-knowers, those who keep Agnihotra.
Vishnu in the form of Agni and others is sung as Brahman at the Veda's beginning. That supreme station of Vishnu is remembered as of the god Savitri.
The great ghee is pressed out; Hari, the Lord, is self-luminous; Parjanya, Vayu and Aditya cook by cold, heat and the rest.
The oblation thrown into the fire rises to the sun; from the sun rain is born; from rain food; then creatures.
Or from the root dha: "dhimahi" — we hold in mind. "Nah" — ours; "bhargah" — of all beings the minds;
may he inspire: may he impel the intellects of the enjoyers in all acts; in the results seen and unseen, he who has the form of Vishnu, Sun and Fire,
impelled by the Lord one goes to heaven or to a pit. "All this is to be dwelt in by the Lord" — Hari, the great and the world;
the god sports with heaven and the rest, "who I am, that Person, the Lord." What is within the sun and called Bharga by those seeking liberation,
for destruction of birth and death and of threefold suffering, this Person is to be seen by meditation in the solar disc.
The truth, being and non-being, consciousness-Brahman, which is Vishnu's supreme abode; the radiance of the god Savitri, the choice, the fourth state;
From the body and the rest, waking, up to Brahman — I am Brahman — we meditate. "He who is that Person in the sun is I, the infinite, Om."
He who ever sets in motion knowledge, good deeds and the rest.
With flame turning to the right, bright as molten gold, with sound like a mass of chariots and clouds, smokeless is the fire;
favorable, fragrant, shaped like a swastika, of clear flame, great-flamed, free of sparks, beneficial;
cats, deer and birds should not pass through the middle. The king should purify his head with earth from a mountain peak,
ears with earth from an anthill top, face with earth from Keshava's temple, neck with earth from Indra's temple, heart with earth from the king's courtyard;
the right arm with earth raised by an elephant's tusk, likewise the left arm with earth raised by a bull's horn;
the back with earth from a lake, the belly with earth from a confluence, the sides with earth from both river banks;
for the king the cleansing of the waist is prescribed with earth from a courtesan's door; the thighs from a sacrifice place, the knees from a cow-pen;
the shanks from a horse-stall, the feet with earth of a chariot wheel; the king seated on a Bhadrasana, the head with pancha-gavya.
Then the four ministers should anoint with pots: from the east with a golden pot full of ghee, the Brahmin;
from the south with a silver pot full of milk, the Kshatriya; with a copper pot with curds, the Vaishya, from the west;
from the north the Shudra minister should anoint with water in a clay pot. Then the consecration of the king, the Rigvedic best Brahmin,
the Chhandoga Brahmin with honey and kusha water should perform; the priest, having gone to the pot holding the stream,
having duly arranged the fire's protection among the assembly, those mantras declared for the king's prosperity-consecration;
with them, great one, one should give, along with Brahmins' chanting. Then the priest should go to the base of the altar;
one should anoint with a hundred-holed golden vessel, saying "Ya oshadhih," "oshadhibhih," "ratha," with scents,
pushpavatih with flowers, "brahmana" with seeds, "ashuh shishanah" with jewels, "ye devah" with kusha water.
